prompt: A parabola has $x$-intercepts at $-3$ and $5$ and passes through the point $(0, -15)$. Its equation can be written as $y = a(x + 3)(x - 5)$. What is the value of $a$?
hint: Substitute the known point into the equation and solve for $a$.

hints.text: Substitute the known point into the equation and solve for $a$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try easier zeros: a parabola with zeros $0$ and $2$ through $(1, -2)$ is $y = a(x)(x-2)$, so $-2 = a(1)(-1)$ and $a = 2$. Substitute the extra point and solve for $a$.

learningObjective: Determine the leading coefficient of a parabola from a point and its zeros.
explanation: The zeros give the factors, but they do not determine the vertical stretch $a$ — a third point does.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why a third point is needed
steps: Infinitely many parabolas share the same two $x$-intercepts — they differ only in how steeply they rise.
The value of $a$ is exactly that steepness, and one extra point pins it down.
This is why the SAT always supplies a third point when it asks you to build a parabola from its zeros.
